title: (CXLD) Wine Confidence 101: Understanding the Basics
location: Montclair Main - Conference Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

This introductory course offers a comprehensive overview of essential wine concepts, designed to establish or strengthen your foundational knowledge and support your ongoing appreciation of wine. 

Over the 5-week course, we will review the primary grape varieties and styles of dry white, rosé, red, and sparkling wines, as well as explore viticulture fundamentals and the winemaking process. We will explore the major wine-producing countries and differences among grape varieties and wine styles. We will review how to taste and critically evaluate wine from visual assessment through aftertaste. For historical context, the course provides an overview of wine’s origins, its evolution, and the business aspects of winemaking. A solid foundation also includes guidance on appropriate tools for opening wine bottles, optimal storage, and serving temperatures to enhance your overall wine experience. 

By the end of the 5-week class, you will have gained a deeper understanding of the many aspects of dry and sparkling wines so you are thoroughly conversant about wine and have tasted between 20 – 25 different wines from around the world!

location: Montclair - Montclair High School, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register. 

Learn the fundamentals of home repair in this practical, hands-on workshop taught by Robert Haas, instructor of the popular Woodworking 101 and Advanced Woodworking classes. Held at Montclair High School, this course gives participants a behind-the-walls look at how common home features are built and maintained.

During the class, Robert will construct two demonstration walls that include doors and a window, showing how these elements are installed and how typical wall structures are assembled. Participants will also learn how traditional double-hung windows operate and how they can be repaired, including basic glass pane replacement.

The workshop will also introduce the basics of residential wiring, demonstrating how outlets and lighting are installed and connected. Throughout the session, Robert will answer questions and offer guidance on a wide range of home repair topics.

Whether you're a homeowner looking to handle basic repairs yourself or simply curious about how things in your home work, this class provides practical knowledge you can use right away.

title: Agentic AI Finance: Governed Metrics, Open Access, Automated Action on Databrick
description:
Cloud Data Driven
Large finance organizations already rely on dashboards and reports, but the real challenge is enabling automation without breaking governance or auditability. This session shares how a global finance organization implemented agent-driven workflows on the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform using Unity Catalog, metrics views, and open lakehouse patterns.

The talk walks through a real implementation where finance metrics are defined once using metrics views, protected with attribute-based access control and automated classification, and reused consistently across reporting, analytics, and automation. Power BI connects directly to governed lakehouse tables and metrics for enterprise reporting, while Iceberg-compliant clients consume Delta tables through Uniform, enabling open access without duplicating data.

Agentic workflows observe certified metrics and events, assist with variance investigation, anomaly triage, and operational follow-ups, and propose actions that remain traceable and reviewable. Early results indicated several hours of manual investigation effort saved per reporting cycle and faster anomaly triage, without introducing additional governance or audit risk. The session includes an architecture walkthrough and demo using synthetic data, reflecting real finance constraints, trade-offs, and lessons learned when moving from reporting to governed, open, and action-oriented analytics.

June 11 – Late Spring Blooming Tree tour – This guided tree identification walk led by Laura Roberts will focus on spring-blooming trees. This is an outdoor tour, so please dress for the weather with appropriate footwear. (Outdoor Program, indoors if inclement weather) 
June 18 – Birds and Art – We’ll learn about some of our favorite resident birds at Van Vleck with Naturalist Jenny Aley and discuss their summer activities. We will also explore our creative side with a simple painting or sketching activity that will help us identify some of our beautiful native birds. No experience necessary – all levels of birders and artists welcome! (Indoor Program) 
June 25th – Mindfulness in the Garden – Jodi Brooks will guide us through very gentle stretching & breathwork, and an outdoor contemplative garden walk. This is a practice of slowing down, cultivating quiet and paying attention to our senses. All levels are welcome. No experience needed. Cold or rainy weather – class will be held indoors, with a short walk outdoors (weather permitting). (Outdoor Program, indoors if inclement weather)

title: Inspiration trap creativity workshop
description:
Live African music and drumming events in NJ
6,7&8pm Issyra Gallery presents - Inspiration Trap Creativity workshop

Only 10 attendees allowed social distancing and mandatory mask wearing.

You are invited to participate in a special session of creative thinking and fresh insight dedicated to inspiration.

We live in a world of constant change that requires us to be able to continually adapt and innovate in order to succeed. Unfortunately, many of us have forgotten how to delve into our raw creativity and leave behind the rigidity of the frameworks we have progressively interiorized.
This unique workshop seeks to reclaim our inspiration and imagination, rethink the unthinkable. It is ideal for people working in the creative arts as well as students, entrepreneurs, team managers, corporate leaders and anyone looking to implement their creative vision.

Inspiration is a vital driving force in our lives that moves us to create our best work and lights the way for new, authentic ideas. How do we invite, cultivate and harness inspiration so that we are able to bring these ideas into reality?
As a self-taught artist exploring various avenues of self-expression, Issa Sow draws a distinction between the phenomenon of inspiration itself and our task of making ourselves ready for it.
In the upcoming Inspiration Trap workshop, we will imagine ways we can invite and contain our inspiration, and well as keep our mind in the open, dynamic state as a receptacle or a “canvas” to collect, reflect and grow our ideas.
Feel free to bring along a personal object, a piece of clothing or even a small piece of furniture to play with during this hands-on experiment in innovative thinking. There are surprises and new elements in each session!

Issa =2
Issa Sow is a contemporary international autodidact artist known as Issa=2.
He believes in life being a journey of continual growth with each new

title: CANCELLED - African Dance for Beginners NEW
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.


	
		
			
			Join us for our all-new African Dance Workshop, an exciting opportunity to move, connect, and celebrate culture through rhythm and community. Led by Karen Miles of Zawadi African Dance and accompanied by two live drummers, this energizing class welcomes dancers of all levels.
			
		
	


The workshop begins with a 10-minute guided warm-up to prepare the body with rhythmic movement and grounding techniques. Participants will then learn Dansa, a vibrant traditional dance of the Malinké people from Upper Guinea.

Dansa is traditionally performed as a joyful celebration during community gatherings, often encouraging collective labor while strengthening unity and fostering a powerful spirit of togetherness. Experience the rich cultural traditions, dynamic rhythms, and uplifting communal energy that make West African dance so inspiring.

Note: This class takes place at DiRasa Gallery, 4 Lackawanna Plaza in Montclair.

title: Open Book, Open Mind; Michael Luo, "Strangers in the Land"
location: Montclair Main - Auditorium, Montclair Main - Conference Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
New Yorker writer and executive editor Michael Luo will talk to Matthew Purdy, editor at large of The New York Times, about about his landmark study, "Strangers in the Land: Exclusion, Belonging, and the Epic Story of the Chinese in America." Co-presented by AAPI New Jersey.

“You can’t paint a complete picture of America without [the story of Chinese Americans], and the New Yorker journalist Michael Luo tells it persuasively in 'Strangers in the Land'... [The book] succeeds through its little biographies of individuals – a range of quirky and fascinating figures, both Chinese and white, who drive the narrative. . . [and offer] a view on the full complexity of American immigration.” —The New York Times Book Review



Doors open at 6 p.m. The discussion will be followed by an audience Q&A and book sales and signing with Watchung Booksellers. 

Open Book / Open Mind is sponsored by Montclair Public Library Foundation, Watchung Booksellers, Anonymous, David and Mary Lee Jones, and our individual Underwriters. We are also grateful for the generous support of our in-kind sponsors, First Congregational Church of Montclair, The George, and Amanti Vino. To support Open Book / Open Mind and other library programs, click here to donate.

title: & Sons at Luna Stage
location: Luna Stage Theatre Company, 555 Valley Road, West Orange, NJ, 07052, United States
description:
Winner of the Kirk Prize for Best New Play, & Sons by Jack Angelo Cummings is a sharply funny, quietly devastating portrait of brotherhood, labor, and the ways men learn—often badly—to love one another. 
On a New Jersey construction site, the DiSanti crew eats subs, burritos, and pizza on their lunch break while everything underneath begins to crack. Dom, the sweet-natured, perpetually high second son, is caught between his best friend Juan, a driven protégé hungry to lead the company, and his older brother Anthony, a imposing, tightly woundvfigure newly returned after years of unexplained absence. As power struggles escalate and old wounds resurface, the men avoid saying what they feel—touching, jostling, and posturing instead, using work and food as cover for grief, loyalty, and longing. By turns hilarious and aching, & Sons is an intimate meditation on masculinity, inheritance, and how blue-collar men translate emotion into action when language fails.

title: Bound/ Unbound: A Queer Quest for Big Love '26
description:
Bound/Unbound is a reimagined riff on Charles L. Mee’s BIG LOVE, exploring the complexities of love, dysfunctional relationships, and the ferocity forged by heartache through a non-binary lens. Originally produced in 2000 as a modern adaptation of THE SUPPLIANTS by Aeschylus, the story of fifty brides who flee to Italy to escape marrying their cousins is expanded in this devised piece to invite queer stories & relationships, and non-binary gender identity & expression. How do we look at the “politics of love and gender” in a more expansive and nuanced way? How does this challenge preconceived notions of love, commitment, and the freedom to choose who and how we love?

title: JOIN US for a walk along  West Essex Trail in Verona
description:
Let's Walk!!
JOIN US for a walk along West Essex Trail in Verona

We will walk a semi-paved path.

We will be walking on a trail in a wooded area, so wear appropriate footwear and clothing. Example - long pants & socks, and you may also want to use bug spray.

We will meet in front of the trail entrance. Park on Fairview Avenue just north of Verona High School, 151 Fairview Ave, Verona, NJ 07044.

West Essex Trail follows a short distance of the former rail bed of the Caldwell Branch on the old Erie-Lackawanna Railroad. The trail runs between the Essex–Passaic county line in Little Falls and Arnold Way in Verona. The trail crosses a trestle over the Peckman River. Although situated in the heavily urbanized part of the state, the trail passes through sections of woodland, providing a short escape from the surrounding congestion.

**Please make sure to RSVP and arrive 5 minutes prior to start time.**

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap. Event will be canceled in the event of extreme weather.

title: Red Baraat in the Amphitheatre
description:
The "infectious" (Rhein Main Press), "cacophonous bhangra funk band from Brooklyn" (The Telegraph) is “the best party band in years” (NPR), and they're coming to Montclair for a free outdoor performance in the Amphitheatre! Join PEAK Performances and Red Baraat for a spring celebration of the year with free ice cream and other free things for Montclair students.
Red Baraat is a pioneering band from Brooklyn, New York. Conceived by dhol player Sunny Jain, the group has drawn worldwide praise for its singular sound, a merging of hard driving Punjabi rhythms with elements of hip-hop, jazz and raw punk energy. The band’s live shows are an unparalleled collision of virtuosity, party, and joy, as Red Baraat reminds us that we are truly all in this together. Red Baraat has toured the globe the past 16 years with stops at Bonnaroo, Austin City Limits, Bumbershoot, New Orleans Jazz Fest, Peter Gabriel’s WOMAD festivals (Australia, New Zealand, Spain, UK), Dubai World Expo 2021, just to name a few. Along the way they sold out rooms as diverse as the Luxembourg Philharmonic and the New York City’s legendary rock club Bowery Ballroom, and performed at the request of The White House (Obama), TED, London Olympic Games, David Byrne, Padma Lakshmi and recent NYC Mayor-elect, Zohran Mamdani. Red Baraat have released 7 albums with numerous accolades from major media outlets and ranked in top 10 lists on Billboard, Apple Music and World Music Charts Europe.

location: Montclair Women’s Club 82 Union St, 82 Union St, Montclair, 07043, United States
description:
Across the country, sex education has become a flashpoint of debate-but what does the evidence actually say? Dr. Eva Goldfarb, Professor of Public Health at MSU is the lead author of a landmark study demonstrating that comprehensive sex ed does much more than preventing unintended pregnancies and STIs. It improves the health and safety and long-term wellbeing of young people. Dr. Goldfarb will discuss the research as well as the growing efforts to restrict access to this info, what’s driving those movements and what it means for our community. Open to All. Light Refreshments available after the talk. Free for MWC, $10 for nonmembers.

title: Bound/ Unbound: A Queer Quest for Big Love '26
description:
Bound/Unbound is a reimagined riff on Charles L. Mee’s BIG LOVE, exploring the complexities of love, dysfunctional relationships, and the ferocity forged by heartache through a non-binary lens. Originally produced in 2000 as a modern adaptation of THE SUPPLIANTS by Aeschylus, the story of fifty brides who flee to Italy to escape marrying their cousins is expanded in this devised piece to invite queer stories & relationships, and non-binary gender identity & expression. How do we look at the “politics of love and gender” in a more expansive and nuanced way? How does this challenge preconceived notions of love, commitment, and the freedom to choose who and how we love?

title: & Sons at Luna Stage
location: Luna Stage Theatre Company, 555 Valley Road, West Orange, NJ, 07052, United States
description:
Winner of the Kirk Prize for Best New Play, & Sons by Jack Angelo Cummings is a sharply funny, quietly devastating portrait of brotherhood, labor, and the ways men learn—often badly—to love one another. 
On a New Jersey construction site, the DiSanti crew eats subs, burritos, and pizza on their lunch break while everything underneath begins to crack. Dom, the sweet-natured, perpetually high second son, is caught between his best friend Juan, a driven protégé hungry to lead the company, and his older brother Anthony, a imposing, tightly woundvfigure newly returned after years of unexplained absence. As power struggles escalate and old wounds resurface, the men avoid saying what they feel—touching, jostling, and posturing instead, using work and food as cover for grief, loyalty, and longing. By turns hilarious and aching, & Sons is an intimate meditation on masculinity, inheritance, and how blue-collar men translate emotion into action when language fails.

title: Lego Robotics for Elementary Students
location: RecRoom, 1 Lackawanna Plaza, Ste. 6, Montclair, 07042, United States
description:
LEGO Robotics for Elementary Kids (Grades K–5) 
LEGO Robotics at Kinetic Minds introduces kids to engineering and beginner coding through hands-on building, testing, and problem-solving using LEGO robotics kits. 
In this small-group, drop-in friendly workshop, kids work in pairs to build real robots, program simple behaviors, and improve their designs through guided challenges. The focus is on curiosity, experimentation, and learning how things work—there’s no single “right” build and no step-by-step cookie-cutter instructions. 
Workshops are intentionally capped at a low student-to-instructor ratio to support collaboration, confidence, and meaningful learning. 
Kids will explore:
• Engineering and building with LEGO robotics components
• Beginner coding concepts (motors, sensors, cause and effect)
• Testing, debugging, and iterating designs
• Teamwork, communication, and explaining ideas 
Details:
• 60-minute session
• Small-group format
• No prior experience required 
Community Sponsorship:
20% of seats are reserved for community sponsorship. Families interested in sponsored spots can email info@kineticmindscreative.com
for details.

title: Casual Volleyball - North Jersey
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More (BVT)
We're a group of people who will start by hitting the ball around for the first 20-30 minutes and then we'll break up into 2-4 teams for two or three hours of play.

If we have more than 20 people show up, we'll break up into three or four teams of 6 (Some may have 7, 8 or 9. Additional players just rotate into play). Games will be to 10 points. Rally scoring. Winner stays on (unless a team has won four straight).

We'll be heading outdoors to the hard court in Leonia off Overpeck County Pk Driveway in the Overpeck County Park.

\*\*\* After playing, we'll be likely heading to Tropical Juice Bar, an idea of regular attendee Kate, for a drink and snack. It's located at 60 River St. in Hackensack. Feel free to join us or suggest another spot for a post-volleyball hangout. \*\*\*

There's no fee to play volleyball and nothing else you need to do besides show up. Come anytime!! All are welcome!!! We're not in a league and are not here to analyze your form. We're more for people who haven't played in months, maybe years, and just want to occasionally play again and hang out.

Directions: You can Google "Volleyball Court in Leonia" and it should come up. Or type 41 Willow Tree Road, Leonia, NJ 07605 into your GPS, but note that it's not on Willow Tree Road, just near it. Instead, turn onto Overpeck County Pk Driveway off Fort Lee Road (Degraw Avenue). It is past the tennis courts and near a basketball court and track. You can try Googling Leonia High School as well. That should help you find it.

We don't have the court reserved and if it happens to be taken, we may play with those already occupying it or we will try to relocate on the fly. It's certainly possible that we may have to cancel that day if we can't find a suitable spot. Please keep that in mind. And if it's looking like it'll rain or snow, I'll make a call on whether to cancel around an hour ahead of time.

Please bring a ball and net if you have them for possible use during the game. Feel free to bring a speaker for music, or snacks and drinks for consumption during play.

If you have trouble finding the court or group, you can call or text Andy Milone at 201-234-9609. There is plenty of parking and an open bathroom at the park.

Hope you'll join us for our 18th volleyball event. Questions or comments? You can message Andy on Meetup, or call/text him at 201-234-9609.

Check out bowling, soccer, volleyball, tennis or one of our other activities at: www.meetup.com/north-jersey-bowling-soccer-volleyball
source: Meetup: NJ Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More

title: [Outside Org]  Aging in Montclair Saturday Social
Bound/ Unbound: A Queer Quest for Big Love '26
description:
Bound/Unbound is a reimagined riff on Charles L. Mee’s BIG LOVE, exploring the complexities of love, dysfunctional relationships, and the ferocity forged by heartache through a non-binary lens. Originally produced in 2000 as a modern adaptation of THE SUPPLIANTS by Aeschylus, the story of fifty brides who flee to Italy to escape marrying their cousins is expanded in this devised piece to invite queer stories & relationships, and non-binary gender identity & expression. How do we look at the “politics of love and gender” in a more expansive and nuanced way? How does this challenge preconceived notions of love, commitment, and the freedom to choose who and how we love?

description:
To honor the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence, the Oratorio Society of New Jersey (OSNJ) will perform America Inspired! – a program dedicated to works of a broad range of American composers. The concert will provide a flavor of the rich melting pot of influences that is American music, including liturgical, spiritual, gospel, jazz, folk, and neo-classical. 
The concert takes place on Saturday, April 25, at 7:30 pm, at Union Congregational Church, 176 Cooper Avenue, Montclair. 
America Inspired! will feature choral and instrumental works by some of our country’s greatest composers, including Samuel Barber, Leonard Bernstein, Aaron Copland, William Dawson, Duke Ellington, George Gershwin and Randall Thompson. 
Tickets are $30 in advance and $35 at the door – plus OSNJ has introduced student pricing: $15 in advance, $20 at the door.
Doors open at 7:00pm for the 7:30pm performance – please arrive early due to General Admission seating. For more information and to purchase tickets online, visit the Oratorio Society of New Jersey website at https://www.oratoriosocietynj.org/.

title: & Sons at Luna Stage
location: Luna Stage Theatre Company, 555 Valley Road, West Orange, NJ, 07052, United States
description:
Winner of the Kirk Prize for Best New Play, & Sons by Jack Angelo Cummings is a sharply funny, quietly devastating portrait of brotherhood, labor, and the ways men learn—often badly—to love one another. 
On a New Jersey construction site, the DiSanti crew eats subs, burritos, and pizza on their lunch break while everything underneath begins to crack. Dom, the sweet-natured, perpetually high second son, is caught between his best friend Juan, a driven protégé hungry to lead the company, and his older brother Anthony, a imposing, tightly woundvfigure newly returned after years of unexplained absence. As power struggles escalate and old wounds resurface, the men avoid saying what they feel—touching, jostling, and posturing instead, using work and food as cover for grief, loyalty, and longing. By turns hilarious and aching, & Sons is an intimate meditation on masculinity, inheritance, and how blue-collar men translate emotion into action when language fails.

title: AAPI NJ Color Run 2026

description:
Join us for a vibrant 5k race and 1-mile fun run in celebration of Holi and Songkran! Holi—the Hindu “Festival of Colors” and “Festival of Spring”—marks the end of winter and honors the triumph of good over evil as people throw colored powder at one another. During Songkran or Thai New Year, people pour water on each other to symbolize washing away the past year’s bad luck and welcoming happiness, renewal, and prosperity. Inspired by these traditions, we are excited to bring the community together for a morning of movement, laughter, and cultural celebration. 
Participants will race through a closed course inside Brookdale Park, getting splattered with colorful powder along the way. Strollers are welcome (though we ask that they start in the back of the pack), but unfortunately, dogs are not permitted.

title: Wissahickon Weird Loop Hike!
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
Join us for this very diverse loop hike, the next in our Wissahickon Watershed series!
This will not only cover the next bit of the Wissahickon Green Ribbon, we will also cover lots of other trails in area parks we haven't done yet.
We meet at the long parking area with the restroom across from the Hawk Watch on St Park Rd in Fort Washington State Park. From here, we'll go slightly south and follow one of the trails in that section of the park.
We will weave around and make our way along some of the trails we did not cover on our previous trip through the area heading east. We'll weave to the north side of the park, and then make our way west to the George Washington Memorial Park.
We'll do nearly a double loop in the big cemetery, and then make our way west to Harriett Wetherill Park. We'll do just about all of the trails there, then make our way south onto a little piece of Cross County Trail, followed by some back streets and community greenways in Plymouth Meeting.
We'll make our way from a neighborhood connection to Dixon Meadows Preserve and do their short trail. A final pleasant back road walk will take us to completed Wissahickon Green Ribbon Trail, which we will follow back to the start.
Distance should be about 15 miles. If needed, contact my cell at 908 343 8374

title: Earth Fest 2026!
location: South Park Street (Bloomfield Ave. and Chruch St.), South Park St., United States
description:
Montclair Township’s Department of Sustainability, the Montclair Center Business Improvement District (BID), and Drive Electric are thrilled to announce the return of Earth Fest, the community’s premier sustainability celebration. The third annual event will take place on Sunday, April 26th, 2026, from 12:00 PM to 4:00 PM at South Street Park (between Bloomfield Avenue and Church Street). 
Building on the success of previous years, Earth Fest 2026 promises an afternoon of education, exploration, and inspiration for residents of all ages. The free event brings together the Montclair community to highlight practical ways residents can adopt more sustainable habits while showcasing the Township’s ongoing efforts to create a more resilient community. 
What to Expect
– Attendees will enjoy a wide array of activities and opportunities to engage with sustainability:
– Live Music Entertainment: Enjoy a full lineup of local and regional musicians performing throughout the afternoon
– Interactive Educational Games & Activities: Learn environmental concepts and best practices through engaging, family-friendly activities
– Vendor & Nonprofit Booths: Discover local businesses and nonprofits leading the charge on sustainable practices and community resilience
– Live Demonstrations: Test-drive eco-friendly alternatives, including electric vehicles, energy-efficient appliances, and other innovative green technologies
– Resource Sharing: Connect with local experts and access information about Montclair’s sustainability programs and initiatives
– Tree Giveaway Pickup: Montclair residents are eligible to receive a free tree! Reserve yours here and pick it up at the event! 
Earth Fest reflects Montclair’s dedication to environmental stewardship and community participation in the transition toward a more sustainable lifestyle. From renewable energy to waste reduction, residents will learn about actionable steps they can take at home and in their neighborhood.

title: Jewish without Apology: A Conversation with Sarah Hurwitz
description:
**Seth Goodchild Memorial Lecture**  
Reception immediately following  
  
Event is at capacity. To be added to the waiting list, contact: Email Aviva Arad, aarad@shomrei.org  
  
**LIVESTREAM  
This event will be livestreamed but NOT recorded. To watch remotely, you must tune in at the time of the event:  http://shomrei.org/live: https://shomrei.org/live**  
  
**About the Program**  
Award-winning author Sarah Hurwitz joins Rabbi Julie Roth for a candid conversation about rediscovering Judaism as an adult and why its intellectual depth and moral clarity feel strikingly relevant to modern life. From finding meaning in a chaotic world to standing tall against rising antisemitism, Sarah explores why embracing Jewish wisdom isn’t just about honoring the past -- it’s about sanctifying the present and elevating our shared humanity.   
  
**Free Babysitting Available**  
Email Aviva Arad, aarad@shomrei.org  
  
**\*Additional parking is available next door at 73 & 77 Park Street.**  
  
**In Loving Memory of Seth Goodchild**   
Seth Goodchild was inspired by his family to convert to Judaism at the end of his life. To honor his legacy and share his love of Judaism, his friends and family sponsored this lecture and a class on exploring Judaism.

title: Mental Health First Aid Training
description:
Mental Health First Aid (MHFA) is an early intervention public education program. It teaches adults how to recognize the signs and symptoms that suggest a potential mental health challenge, how to listen nonjudgmentally and give reassurance to a person who may be experiencing a mental health challenge, and how to refer a person to appropriate professional support and services.

 

The Mental Health Association's Intensive Family Support Services(IFSS) provides support to family members of adults living with mental health conditions. IFSS staff, Eileen Strungis and Mel Bryan, will be offering an in-person course Monday, April 27th, from 10:00am-5:00pm at the Montclair Public Library.  Workbooks covering the material and lunch will be provided for all attendees. There is no cost to participate, but seats are limited. 

 

If you would like to join us for this interactive, evidence-based course to learn valuable skills to assist those living with mental health challenges, please reach out to Eileen at estrungis@mhainspire.org, or reply to this email for next steps.

title: [MILL @ MPL] Taste of Tai Chi
description:
Note: This is a class run through the MILL. Please register through their website here.


T'ai Chi Ch'uan is a 1000 year old art of mind-body health and energy cultivation. “A Taste of Tai Chi” introduces students to the 12-posture Yang-style Short Form of Master Bow Sim Mark and is designed for students of all ages and levels of physical ability. No prior experience with T'ai Chi is necessary. The health benefits of T'ai Chi include balance, flexibility, strength, immune-system support, and stress relief.

LEWIS FREEMAN studied the “Taste of T’ai Chi” form with Don Madison (Dragon T'ai Chi Ch'uan Association) and achieved the level of Assistant Teacher in July 2019. He previously studied the Yang-style short form at Long River T’aiChi Circle in Manhattan in the 1990s. When he's not practicing T’ai Chi, Lewis teaches at Fordham University as Senior Lecturer in Communication and Media Studies and also consults for businesses and organizations.

Also about realising that sometimes compromise is unnecessary because it’s just me needing to get out of my own way and the tactics I use to do exactly that.

Mary J Jay (JJ) is a software engineer who’s been working with WordPress for over 15 years. She currently works as a contract staff engineer at Vox Media where the person she needs to compromise with the most to deliver good software on time is herself.

title: Denim Day 2026: Mind the Gaps, Move Forward
description:
April is Sexual Assault Awareness Month, and together, we can break the silence. The Montclair State University Police Department and the Office of Advocacy & Outreach are committed to fostering a campus where survivors feel heard, supported, and empowered. It starts with believing. It starts with you. By offering a safe and affirming response to those who disclose gender-based and sexual violence, we can create lasting change. Let’s stand together to end the cycle of silence—because every voice matters, and every action counts.
Denim Day is recognized internationally as a day of action and awareness, encouraging people to wear denim to challenge victim-blaming and educate others about sexual violence. This year, Denim Day falls on Wednesday, April 29, 2026.
The University Police and Office of Advocacy & Outreach and the Office of Advocacy and Community Resilience, in partnership with over 30 campus and local community organizations, invites you to join us from 9 a.m. to 12 p.m. at the Amphitheater for a powerful awareness event honoring survivors and increasing awareness of available resources.
Despite the gaps that still exist in the criminal justice system, in resources, and in prevention education, we will move forward together as a community. As part of this commitment, we will walk one mile around campus in solidarity with survivors.

Hosted by: Advocacy and Outreach

title: Weekly Labyrinth Walks, Wednesdays 11am-1pm
description: Weekly: Wednesdays 11am-1pm in the Sanctuary  Take your soul for a walk on the labyrinth.  We are pleased to offer labyrinth walks each Wednesday in the mid-day as a chance to connect with your soul in our beautiful sanctuary. The labyrinth is an ancient spiritual tool , a mode of “walking prayer” that invites us to go deeper in our walk with God.  Our labyrinth, modeled on one in Chartes Cathedral in France, sits as the center of our Sanctuary, a constant metaphor for our spiritual lives.  Just like the labyrinth, our lives are not linear, but filled with twists and turns.  Sometimes we make great progress, and other times we feel we are going backwards.  But if we trust in the path we will find ourselves in the center -- the heart of God. All are welcome to take their souls out for a healing walk... no experience necessary!  Check out this lovely write up on Baristanet from the Spring 2014. Watch this video to find out more about walking the labyrinth. If you’ve never done so come out one Wednesday evening and give it a try. It is a wonderful way to nourish your soul and spend some quiet time in prayer or meditation.

title: (CXLD) Wine Confidence 101: Understanding the Basics
location: Montclair Main - Conference Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

This introductory course offers a comprehensive overview of essential wine concepts, designed to establish or strengthen your foundational knowledge and support your ongoing appreciation of wine. 

Over the 5-week course, we will review the primary grape varieties and styles of dry white, rosé, red, and sparkling wines, as well as explore viticulture fundamentals and the winemaking process. We will explore the major wine-producing countries and differences among grape varieties and wine styles. We will review how to taste and critically evaluate wine from visual assessment through aftertaste. For historical context, the course provides an overview of wine’s origins, its evolution, and the business aspects of winemaking. A solid foundation also includes guidance on appropriate tools for opening wine bottles, optimal storage, and serving temperatures to enhance your overall wine experience. 

By the end of the 5-week class, you will have gained a deeper understanding of the many aspects of dry and sparkling wines so you are thoroughly conversant about wine and have tasted between 20 – 25 different wines from around the world!

Participants will explore Gemini’s GEMs and image generation capabilities, as well as Claude’s artifacts and strengths in analyzing and generating longer-form content.

location: Montclair - Montclair High School, Montclair Public Library
description:

Learn the fundamentals of home repair in this practical, hands-on workshop taught by Robert Haas, instructor of the popular Woodworking 101 and Advanced Woodworking classes. Held at Montclair High School, this course gives participants a behind-the-walls look at how common home features are built and maintained.

During the class, Robert will construct two demonstration walls that include doors and a window, showing how these elements are installed and how typical wall structures are assembled. Participants will also learn how traditional double-hung windows operate and how they can be repaired, including basic glass pane replacement.

The workshop will also introduce the basics of residential wiring, demonstrating how outlets and lighting are installed and connected. Throughout the session, Robert will answer questions and offer guidance on a wide range of home repair topics.

Whether you're a homeowner looking to handle basic repairs yourself or simply curious about how things in your home work, this class provides practical knowledge you can use right away.

title: Implementing Zero Trust Security Architectures: Federated vs Centralized
description:
Cloud Data Driven
🔐 **Securing modern data systems** is no longer about boundaries - it is about trust, identity, and control.

As enterprise data ecosystems expand across hybrid and multi-cloud environments, traditional perimeter-based security models are no longer sufficient to protect sensitive information. Organizations are increasingly adopting Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) to secure complex data environments where information flows across distributed platforms, services, and organizational boundaries.

💡 **In this session**, we explore how Zero Trust principles can be applied to modern enterprise data architectures, focusing on the security implications of federated and centralized data models.

🔍 **What will be covered:**

🔹 How federated and centralized architectures handle identity management
🔹 Approaches to access control in distributed environments
🔹 Data governance strategies within a Zero Trust framework

⚖️ **Architectural trade-offs:**

🔹 Federated architectures support data sovereignty, localized policy enforcement, and distributed resilience
🔹 Centralized architectures enable unified security policies, centralized monitoring, and coordinated threat response

**🤖 AI and Zero Trust:**

🔹 Real-time threat detection powered by AI
🔹 Behavioral analytics for anomaly identification
🔹 Automated response mechanisms to mitigate risks

**🛡️ Protecting modern data pipelines:**

🔹 Securing AI-powered data pipelines end-to-end
🔹 Maintaining data lineage visibility across systems
🔹 Ensuring compliance with evolving regulatory requirements

**🎯 Learning objectives:**

🔹 Design secure and scalable enterprise data systems
🔹 Understand the trade-offs between federated and centralized models
🔹 Implement Zero Trust strategies for stronger data protection in AI-enabled environments

**📊 Level:** Intermediate

**📅 Date/Time:** Thursday, Apr 30 · 12:00 PM EST

🎤 **Speaker:** Vineel Bala - Director, Database Administration at Fidelity Investments. Contact: 👉 https://www.linkedin.com/in/vineel-bala-434250101/

description:

6,7&8pm Issyra Gallery presents - Inspiration Trap Creativity workshop

Only 10 attendees allowed social distancing and mandatory mask wearing.

You are invited to participate in a special session of creative thinking and fresh insight dedicated to inspiration.

We live in a world of constant change that requires us to be able to continually adapt and innovate in order to succeed. Unfortunately, many of us have forgotten how to delve into our raw creativity and leave behind the rigidity of the frameworks we have progressively interiorized.
This unique workshop seeks to reclaim our inspiration and imagination, rethink the unthinkable. It is ideal for people working in the creative arts as well as students, entrepreneurs, team managers, corporate leaders and anyone looking to implement their creative vision.

Inspiration is a vital driving force in our lives that moves us to create our best work and lights the way for new, authentic ideas. How do we invite, cultivate and harness inspiration so that we are able to bring these ideas into reality?
As a self-taught artist exploring various avenues of self-expression, Issa Sow draws a distinction between the phenomenon of inspiration itself and our task of making ourselves ready for it.
In the upcoming Inspiration Trap workshop, we will imagine ways we can invite and contain our inspiration, and well as keep our mind in the open, dynamic state as a receptacle or a “canvas” to collect, reflect and grow our ideas.
Feel free to bring along a personal object, a piece of clothing or even a small piece of furniture to play with during this hands-on experiment in innovative thinking. There are surprises and new elements in each session!

Issa =2
Issa Sow is a contemporary international autodidact artist known as Issa=2.
He believes in life being a journey of continual growth with each new

title: Queer Lit Club
description:
This month we'll be reading  "Stag Dance" by Torrey Peters.

"In Stag Dance, the titular novel, a group of restless lumberjacks working in an illegal winter logging outfit plan a dance that some of them will volunteer to attend as women. When the broadest, strongest, plainest of the axmen announces his intention to dance as a woman, he finds himself caught in a strange rivalry with a pretty young jack, provoking a cascade of obsession, jealousy, and betrayal that will culminate on the big night in an astonishing vision of gender and transition. Three startling stories surround Stag Dance: "Infect Your Friends and Loved Ones" imagines a gender apocalypse brought about by an unstable ex-girlfriend. In "The Chaser," a secret romance between roommates at a Quaker boarding school brings out intrigue and cruelty. In the last story, "The Masker," a party weekend on the Las Vegas strip turns dark when a young crossdresser must choose between two guides: a handsome mystery man who objectifies her in thrilling ways, or a cynical veteran trans woman offering unglamorous sisterhood."

title: CANCELLED - African Dance for Beginners NEW
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.


	
		
			
			Join us for our all-new African Dance Workshop, an exciting opportunity to move, connect, and celebrate culture through rhythm and community. Led by Karen Miles of Zawadi African Dance and accompanied by two live drummers, this energizing class welcomes dancers of all levels.
			
		
	


The workshop begins with a 10-minute guided warm-up to prepare the body with rhythmic movement and grounding techniques. Participants will then learn Dansa, a vibrant traditional dance of the Malinké people from Upper Guinea.

Dansa is traditionally performed as a joyful celebration during community gatherings, often encouraging collective labor while strengthening unity and fostering a powerful spirit of togetherness. Experience the rich cultural traditions, dynamic rhythms, and uplifting communal energy that make West African dance so inspiring.

Note: This class takes place at DiRasa Gallery, 4 Lackawanna Plaza in Montclair.

title: Open Book, Open Mind; Daniel Okrent, "Art Ain't Easy"
description:
Daniel Okrent, a distinguished journalist and author, talks with Alexandra Jacobs of The New York Times Book Review about the complex inner world of one of the 20th century’s most beloved theatrical composers. Part of Yale University Press's Jewish Lives series. " I have had the same conversation with three musical theater fan friends, where we started out wondering what else we needed to know about Sondheim but found Okrent’s book a marvelous feast full of new insights. And if you’re a newbie, Okrent’s book is a great place to begin. As Noël Coward put it in his delightful 'I Went to a Marvelous Party,' I couldn’t have liked it more."―John McWhorter, The New York Times

Presented in collaboration with the Montclair Literary Festival. No registration required. 

The discussion will be followed by an audience Q&A and book sales and signing with Watchung Booksellers. 

Open Book / Open Mind is sponsored by Montclair Public Library Foundation, Watchung Booksellers, Anonymous, David and Mary Lee Jones, and our individual Underwriters. We are also grateful for the generous support of our in-kind sponsors, First Congregational Church of Montclair, The George, and Amanti Vino. title: NJ Code & Coffee - May meetup
description:
NJ Code & Coffee
Calling all New Jersey techies to the **NJ Code and Coffee** tech community meetup at the EqualSpace ES550 Tech & Innovation campus!

Code and Coffee is an inclusive, informal networking/co-working session for those in tech (and the tech-curious).
That includes operators, founders, and investors. Developers, data engineers, UX/UI designers, data scientists, product managers, software engineers, solution architects... **all are welcome!**

People of all skill and experience levels can attend, we love it that way. Many people (optionally) bring projects to work on, and many other people (optionally) socialize the entire time. It's entirely up to you!

Come grab a cup of coffee and meet new people, share stories, find collaborators, talk about everything tech, talk about everything NOT tech, take a break from job applications, get away from the computer screen, make connections, make conversation, **make friends!**

**Agenda:**
**2pm:** Doors open, networking starts
**2:30pm:** Intro circle
**3pm:** networking continues
**5pm:** event ends

**The Intro Circle**
**Near the beginning of the event (about 2:30 pm), we will do a standup in a circle:**
We first talk about organizer announcements, updates, and logistics. Then we go around the circle where each person says:

*your name and job title/ role in tech/ tech stack,
- What you can help others with,
*What you would like help with,
- Job opportunities you're hiring for OR announce that you are looking for one. If none, that's cool.

After the introduction circle, everything is self-organized.

**Community Discord - come hang out before and after!:**
[www.codeandcoffee.chat](www.codeandcoffee.chat)

**The Venue**
Equal Space is a premium share-space created with multicultural business owners in mind, =SPACE equips founders with resources, programming and a powerful network.

Headquartered in the City of Newark, their share-space provides resources for startups, coaching for tech companies, and a wealth of intellectuals to collaborate and build with. The next wave in enterprises is being born within their walls. Become a part of the story: [EqualSpace.co/](https://equalspace.co/)

title: New Jersey Restaurant & Hospitality Association: ServSafe Food Safety Manager Course & Exam
description: ServSafe Food Safety Manager Training and Certification is required by law in the state of New Jersey. Currently, the state law requires that at least one person per establishment be ServSafe Food Safety Manager-certified. Classes are taught in one day—you take both the class and the exam in the same day.The class will run from 9am to 5pm with a break for lunch. Be sure to arrive on time with a #2 pencil and a photo ID. You will need a 70% or above in order to pass the test. Since ServSafe is now offering electronic certificates, please ensure that you provide a valid email address on the answer sheet. You will receive your certificate via email within 2-3 weeks. description: Weekly: Wednesdays 11am-1pm in the Sanctuary  Take your soul for a walk on the labyrinth.  We are pleased to offer labyrinth walks each Wednesday in the mid-day as a chance to connect with your soul in our beautiful sanctuary. The labyrinth is an ancient spiritual tool , a mode of “walking prayer” that invites us to go deeper in our walk with God.  Our labyrinth, modeled on one in Chartes Cathedral in France, sits as the center of our Sanctuary, a constant metaphor for our spiritual lives.  Just like the labyrinth, our lives are not linear, but filled with twists and turns.  Sometimes we make great progress, and other times we feel we are going backwards.  But if we trust in the path we will find ourselves in the center -- the heart of God. All are welcome to take their souls out for a healing walk... no experience necessary!  Check out this lovely write up on Baristanet from the Spring 2014. Watch this video to find out more about walking the labyrinth. If you’ve never done so come out one Wednesday evening and give it a try. It is a wonderful way to nourish your soul and spend some quiet time in prayer or meditation.

title: (CXLD) Wine Confidence 101: Understanding the Basics
location: Montclair Main - Conference Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

This introductory course offers a comprehensive overview of essential wine concepts, designed to establish or strengthen your foundational knowledge and support your ongoing appreciation of wine. 

Over the 5-week course, we will review the primary grape varieties and styles of dry white, rosé, red, and sparkling wines, as well as explore viticulture fundamentals and the winemaking process. We will explore the major wine-producing countries and differences among grape varieties and wine styles. We will review how to taste and critically evaluate wine from visual assessment through aftertaste. For historical context, the course provides an overview of wine’s origins, its evolution, and the business aspects of winemaking. A solid foundation also includes guidance on appropriate tools for opening wine bottles, optimal storage, and serving temperatures to enhance your overall wine experience. 

By the end of the 5-week class, you will have gained a deeper understanding of the many aspects of dry and sparkling wines so you are thoroughly conversant about wine and have tasted between 20 – 25 different wines from around the world!

description:

Using AI as a thinking partner—not a replacement for expertise

Held at Montclair High School, this course gives participants a behind-the-walls look at how common home features are built and maintained.

During the class, Robert will construct two demonstration walls that include doors and a window, showing how these elements are installed and how typical wall structures are assembled. Participants will also learn how traditional double-hung windows operate and how they can be repaired, including basic glass pane replacement.

The workshop will also introduce the basics of residential wiring, demonstrating how outlets and lighting are installed and connected. Throughout the session, Robert will answer questions and offer guidance on a wide range of home repair topics.

Whether you're a homeowner looking to handle basic repairs yourself or simply curious about how things in your home work, this class provides practical knowledge you can use right away.

title: Inspiration trap creativity workshop
description:

Only 10 attendees allowed social distancing and mandatory mask wearing.

You are invited to participate in a special session of creative thinking and fresh insight dedicated to inspiration.

We live in a world of constant change that requires us to be able to continually adapt and innovate in order to succeed. Unfortunately, many of us have forgotten how to delve into our raw creativity and leave behind the rigidity of the frameworks we have progressively interiorized.
This unique workshop seeks to reclaim our inspiration and imagination, rethink the unthinkable. It is ideal for people working in the creative arts as well as students, entrepreneurs, team managers, corporate leaders and anyone looking to implement their creative vision.

Inspiration is a vital driving force in our lives that moves us to create our best work and lights the way for new, authentic ideas. How do we invite, cultivate and harness inspiration so that we are able to bring these ideas into reality?
As a self-taught artist exploring various avenues of self-expression, Issa Sow draws a distinction between the phenomenon of inspiration itself and our task of making ourselves ready for it.
In the upcoming Inspiration Trap workshop, we will imagine ways we can invite and contain our inspiration, and well as keep our mind in the open, dynamic state as a receptacle or a “canvas” to collect, reflect and grow our ideas.
Feel free to bring along a personal object, a piece of clothing or even a small piece of furniture to play with during this hands-on experiment in innovative thinking. There are surprises and new elements in each session!

Issa =2
Issa Sow is a contemporary international autodidact artist known as Issa=2.

title: Bowling Night - North Jersey
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More (BVT)
This is an event for casual bowling at Montvale Lanes, 14 W. Grand Ave. All are welcome for **two games, food and drinks**, and any post- or pre-game hang out. Show up anytime! Questions or comments? You can message Andy Milone on Meetup, or call/text him at **201-234-9609**.

\*\*\* Before bowling, we might stop by the Pizza Parlour, 6 S. Kinderkamack Road in Montvale, for a few slices. Post a comment on the event page to gauge interest. **After bowling, we'll definitely be heading to Davey's Irish Pub & Restaurant, 5 Park St. in Montvale, or The Ridge Diner, 125 Kinderkamack Road in Park Ridge, at 10 p.m. for some food and/or drinks.** \*\*\*

About the group: People of all ages, backgrounds and abilities are welcome! We're not professionals and we're not in a league. In fact, we're a group of people who probably each won't score more than 100 points and will land more than our fair share of gutter balls. There's no pressure at all!!!! We're not here to analyze your form or technique.

More event details: You pay for your own games, food and drinks. Please bring cash. The alley does not accept card. But there is an ATM on site. **The** **cost per player is $18 for two games** **and bowling shoes.** If you have your own shoes, the cost is $12. Please try to bring exact change since Andy will have a limited amount of cash. If you bring a $20 bill and he doesn't have change, any remainder would just go toward the bowling alley tip.

Food and drinks (alcoholic and non-alcoholic) are available on site, plus tables and an alley bar to hang at during the event. There is a dart board and a few arcade games, as well.

**What do you do when you get there?** First, find the group inside around the front desk. Look for a growing group of people! Call or text Andy Milone at 201-234-9609 if you can't find us. Once Andy secures the lanes, please pay him before getting your bowling shoes.

**Please know that it is possible we have to wait 20-40 minutes until lane(s) free up.** It's also possible that we may have to relocate or cancel that night if there's a long wait list upon arrival. Please keep that in mind if traveling from far away!

For those who don't have cars or are looking to avoid driving, the Montvale Train Station is only like a five-minute walk from the bowling alley and can be reached via the Pascack Valley Line. Last train leaves at 12:20 a.m. and heads toward Hoboken. (https://gmtma.org/wp-content/uploads/2011/11/rail_system_map.jpg)

Many thanks to Taylor, one of our group participants, for recommending Montvale Lanes! You can learn more at: www.montvalelanes.com.

Hope you'll join us for our 23rd bowling event, or consider attending one of our volleyball, ping pong, skating or other activities -> www.meetup.com/north-jersey-bowling-soccer-volleyball
source: Meetup: NJ Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More

title: Hike w/ Kirk of RRWA! 3-4 mi
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Saturday, May 9, 10am - 12:30 pm

Click to register: https://rahwayriver.org/calendar.html

Free expert-led hike in South Mountain Reservation
Hike about 2-3 hours covering 3-4 miles at a modest pace over rocky trails with one long climb from the
Rahway River up South Mountain.

Focus on ecology and hydrology, led by Dr. Kirk Barrett, President of the Rahway
Watershed Association and expert on local watershed issues.

Good balance required. Children welcome.
No dogs. Sponsered by South Mountain Conservancy and the Rahway River Watershed Association. Meet at Clipper Pavilion in South
Mountain Reservation on Cherry Lane in West Orange. Advance registration required via rahwayriver.org/calendar.html . Email
president@rahwayriver.org with questions.

Please come to the starting point 10 minutes ahead of time so the hike can start promptly. Times are our best estimates; they can vary depending on conditions, and the size and pace of a group. title: Noontime Cornhole - North Jersey
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More (BVT)
Come hang with us for two to three hours of casual cornhole at a local park.

The gathering is tentatively scheduled for Lodi Memorial Park, behind the library, 1 Memorial Dr., because the area has four permanent concrete boards.

There is not a ton of parking, but there is a huge lot across the street as part of the shopping plaza.

Comment below if you have your own boards and beanbags, or if you want to bring another yard game. A volleyball court and basketball court, as well as turf field, are also on site. If anyone knows of any other permanent cornhole setups in North Jersey, feel free to also make that suggestion. We may relocate as a result.

\*\*\* After playing, we'll likely be heading somewhere for a drink and snack. Feel free to suggest a spot for a post-cornhole hangout. \*\*\*

There's no fee to play and nothing else you need to do besides show up. Come anytime!! All are welcome!!! We're not in a league and are not here to analyze your form. We're here for people who haven't played in months, maybe years, and just want to occasionally play and hang out.

The event comes to you courtesy of prior suggestions for future events and our group's WhatsApp chat.

Hope you'll join us for our first cornhole event. Questions or comments? You can message Andy on Meetup, or call/text him at 201-234-9609.
Check out bowling, soccer, volleyball, tennis, skating or one of our other activities at: [www.meetup.com/north-jersey-bowling-soccer-volleyball](https://www.meetup.com/north-jersey-bowling-soccer-volleyball)

title: Midday MeetUp - Blueberries, New Jersey’s Wonder Fruit
description:
**Midday MeetUp - Blueberries, New Jersey’s Wonder Fruit**   
A monthly gathering to make connections and learn together.  
11:45am Catered Lunch (free)  
12:30pm Featured Program   
  
Speaker: Food historian, Judith Krall-Russo  
  
The cultivated blueberry has its roots in the Pinelands of New Jersey. Elizabeth White along with Dr. Fredrick Coville, proved that the “swamp huckleberry” could be cultivated. Learn the history of this fascinating berry and the contributions Elizabeth White of Whitesbog made to their cultivation. Today the blueberry is touted as the wonder fruit with a host of healthful benefits. Learn about the history, health benefits and a variety of ways to prepare and savor these berries.

title: Weekly Labyrinth Walks, Wednesdays 11am-1pm
description: Weekly: Wednesdays 11am-1pm in the Sanctuary  Take your soul for a walk on the labyrinth.  We are pleased to offer labyrinth walks each Wednesday in the mid-day as a chance to connect with your soul in our beautiful sanctuary. The labyrinth is an ancient spiritual tool , a mode of “walking prayer” that invites us to go deeper in our walk with God.  Our labyrinth, modeled on one in Chartes Cathedral in France, sits as the center of our Sanctuary, a constant metaphor for our spiritual lives.  Just like the labyrinth, our lives are not linear, but filled with twists and turns.  Sometimes we make great progress, and other times we feel we are going backwards.  But if we trust in the path we will find ourselves in the center -- the heart of God. All are welcome to take their souls out for a healing walk... no experience necessary!  Check out this lovely write up on Baristanet from the Spring 2014. Watch this video to find out more about walking the labyrinth. If you’ve never done so come out one Wednesday evening and give it a try. It is a wonderful way to nourish your soul and spend some quiet time in prayer or meditation.

title: Silent Failures in AI Data Systems: Risk Drift in Pipelines​
description:
Cloud Data Driven
As AI becomes embedded in cloud data platforms, organizations are encountering failure modes that differ fundamentally from traditional deterministic systems. In contrast to binary failures, AI-augmented pipelines often degrade silently, with quality erosion emerging gradually and compounding over time.

This talk explores key failure patterns in production AI data systems. Drawing from machine learning systems research, we examine how data and concept drift can persist undetected as models continue producing outputs despite shifting feature distributions. The risk intensifies in chained pipelines, where probabilistic errors compound across stages—for example, when upstream model inaccuracies propagate and amplify downstream.

We also analyze non-deterministic inference behavior, which complicates reproducibility, auditability, and root cause analysis in cloud environments. The session highlights risks of AI-generated data contamination, where synthetic outputs are mistakenly treated as ground truth, accelerating feedback loops and long-term model degradation.

At the infrastructure level, we discuss challenges such as non-linear inference cost scaling, observability gaps that mask semantic failures, and automation complacency that reduces human oversight.

The talk concludes with practical design principles for cloud data systems, including metadata-first architectures, explicit trust boundaries, and human-in-the-loop checkpoints to build resilient, auditable, and trustworthy AI-driven pipelines.

title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**

A gentle, grounding Forest Therapy experience designed to help you slow down, connect with nature, and restore your senses. We will remain within a mile of our starting point at Tulip Springs, moving only short distances as needed for comfort and exploration.

title: SQL Server 2025: The Future of Data Starts Here
description:
Cloud Data Driven
SQL Server 2025 is more than just an upgrade—it’s a leap forward. From becoming an AI-ready database to delivering modern development tools, this release is packed with innovations that redefine performance, scalability, and productivity.

In this session, you’ll see demos and practical examples showcasing a wide range of enhancements, including:

Improved JSON handling
T‑SQL REST API integration
Expanded T‑SQL functionality, including fuzzy string matching and regular expression support
Time‑bound Extended Events
Change event streaming for real‑time data integration
Mirroring in Microsoft Fabric
Updates to change tracking and columnstore indexes

Whether you’re a developer, DBA, or architect, this session will help you understand where SQL Server 2025 fits into your broader data platform strategy. Join us to explore what’s new and improved in SQL Server 2025!

title: Centralized Data Lakes in the Cloud: Scalable and Governed Architectures
description:
Cloud Data Driven
Global data creation is projected to reach 175 zettabytes, with enterprises managing the majority of this growth. In data-intensive industries, organizations process an average of 9.1 petabytes per enterprise, exposing the limitations of traditional data warehouses. Yet 76% of organizations struggle with data lake governance, and 68% lack clear data ownership.

This session presents a research-backed framework for building centralized, cloud-based data lakes that deliver measurable improvements in performance, cost, and governance. Mature implementations achieve 3.2× faster time-to-insight, 54% reduction in data preparation effort, and 59.3% lower storage costs. Multi-layered architectures improve query performance by 73%, increase resource utilization by 81%, and reduce bottlenecks by 67.4%.

Cloud-native distributed storage supports 3.2× higher performance for mixed workloads, enables 8.7× more concurrent users, and delivers 99.99% availability. Beyond architecture, strong governance and master data management reduce inconsistencies by 83.6%, increase data utilization by 412%, and improve decision-making speed by 47.2%.

Security-by-design approaches reduce unauthorized access by 78.4%, lower breach likelihood by 56.2%, and decrease compliance penalties by 85.4%.

Attendees will gain practical, data-driven strategies to design scalable, secure, and governance-centric cloud data lakes.

title: Help Desk - Bring Your Laptop, Yourself, and Your WordPress Problems
description:
WordPress Montclair Meetup
If you are running a WordPress site and are having issues and would like some help, then this Meetup is for you!

If you know some things, expert or not, and want to give back to the WordPress community, then this Meetup is for you too!

We will do our best to match a problem with a problem-solver. On-site and in real-time. Just bring yourself, your laptop, and your WordPress problems.

It's OK if you attend and only want to observe. We recognize this is how people learn. Given our time limit of two hours, we may not be able to solve everyone's issues, but we will try! If you are seeking help, please come prepared. Have your web site loaded in a browser, have your WordPress admin ready, along with a short list of issues you are trying to solve.

People helping are volunteers and may not be experts. There is risk to breaking your site! Please do not bring client or business sites that can impact reputations or revenue. If you have a staging site we can test things with, that is always preferred. If it is a production site, please create a site backup before having someone do any work on your site.

If you cannot find the group, please ask the front desk where the WordPress meetup group is meeting.

**PARKING**:
We've been asked to not park in the United Way lot behind the library as it could result in a parking ticket. Please find street parking or a parking deck.

\-\-\-
Join the **JerseyPress Slack** group to chat with others in our community and get help: [https://jerseypress.org/slack/](https://jerseypress.org/slack/)

JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.

We will hike for about an hour - 3.5 miles. We will be walking on trails in the woods, so appropriate footwear, long pants & socks, and bug spray.

Will will meet at:
[https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7](https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7) Eagle Rock Trail Parking Lot by Kiosk#1

If you enter from Eagle Rock Way, go pass the Highlawn and stay left. There will be a parking lot at the end of the curve to your right.

Eagle Rock Reservation is 408 acres of hills, streams, and valleys located on the borders of West Orange, Verona, and Montclair, New Jersey. Though located in the middle of the most densely populated county in the most densely populated state in the country, the Reservation is mostly undeveloped and boasts an extensive trail system within its borders.

**Please make sure to RSVP and arrive 5 minutes prior to start time.**

FOLLOW US ON INSTAGRAM - letswalkmeetup

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap. Event will be canceled in the event of extreme weather.

title: Weekly Labyrinth Walks, Wednesdays 11am-1pm
description: Weekly: Wednesdays 11am-1pm in the Sanctuary  Take your soul for a walk on the labyrinth.  We are pleased to offer labyrinth walks each Wednesday in the mid-day as a chance to connect with your soul in our beautiful sanctuary. The labyrinth is an ancient spiritual tool , a mode of “walking prayer” that invites us to go deeper in our walk with God.  Our labyrinth, modeled on one in Chartes Cathedral in France, sits as the center of our Sanctuary, a constant metaphor for our spiritual lives.  Just like the labyrinth, our lives are not linear, but filled with twists and turns.  Sometimes we make great progress, and other times we feel we are going backwards.  But if we trust in the path we will find ourselves in the center -- the heart of God. All are welcome to take their souls out for a healing walk... no experience necessary!  Check out this lovely write up on Baristanet from the Spring 2014. Watch this video to find out more about walking the labyrinth. If you’ve never done so come out one Wednesday evening and give it a try. It is a wonderful way to nourish your soul and spend some quiet time in prayer or meditation.

title: Midday MeetUp - Bonnie Rapp, Best of Broadway
description:
**Midday MeetUp - Bonnie Rapp, Best of Broadway   
A monthly gathering to make connections and learn together.  
11:45am Catered Lunch (free)  
12:30pm Featured Program   
  
Experience *The Best of Broadway* as Bonnie Rapp brings to life unforgettable moments from Tony Award–winning musicals. Relive the golden age of musical theatre through beloved classics and timeless melodies by legendary composers such as Rodgers and Hammerstein, Lerner and Loewe, Frank Loesser, Irving Berlin and more!  
  
Cost:** FREE or Suggested Donation of $10 per person to offset costs. (Bill My Account is only open to Shomrei Members)  
  
**RSVP:** Required so we know how much food to buy.  
https://shomrei.easyshul.com/events/6967e6f2368f110026c0c486  
  
**\***Members & PreSchool Families should use their fob to access the building.  
 About Bonnie Rapp**  
Bonnie had the honor of performing the lead role of Christine Daaé in the National Tour/San Francisco Company of Andrew Lloyd Webber's The Phantom of the Opera. Some of Bonnie’s favorite roles include Maria in The Sound of Music, Kate in Kiss Me, Kate, Cinderella in Rodgers and Hammerstein’s Cinderella, Louise in Gypsy and Sister Amnesia and Sister Leo in Nunsense, Nunsense II and Nunsense Jamboree. In addition, Bonnie has appeared in numerous galas, fundraisers, and Broadway concerts, including performances at Lincoln Center's Avery Fisher Hall.  
  
For the past decade, Bonnie has devoted her talents to providing live musical entertainment for a wide range of audiences, including corporate and community events, libraries, private celebrations, JCCs, and residents of independent living, assisted living, nursing homes, and memory care communities.  
  
Full_Season_Schedule_for_Midday_MeetUps: https://shomrei.org/calendar/midday-meetup-calendar

title: Ping Pong Party - North Jersey
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More (BVT)
We're a group of people who will casually hit the ball around and rotate playing to 10 or 15 points for two to three hours. If there's an interest, we may do king of the hill, round robin, a small tournament or some other organized game.

All are welcome!! It's just casual fun! Come anytime! We're not in a league and are not here to analyze your form.

We'll be heading indoors to the table tennis tables at Ready to Golf, 3 New Bridge Road in River Edge. We'll likely have pizza delivered or hang out some more at Coach House Diner, 55 Rte 4 in Hackensack.

Ready to Golf has a lot to offer, including rentable table tennis tables, and comes as a recommendation of Joe, one of our many regulars.

We'll be reserving five or six tables for singles and doubles play but we will get more if more than 20 people show up or they're available.

The rental price covers paddles and balls. Final pricing will be somewhere in the neighborhood of $10-15 per person. Please bring cash to pay for what you owe! We'll settle the bill before play.

For planning purposes, we also ask that if you're stopping by later than 8 p.m., that you please let me know by commenting below, or calling or texting me.

There is a snack bar on site, but it's only open until 7:30 p.m. There are some bottled drinks available and a water fountain, but you're welcome to bring food and beverages from the outside. It's BYOB friendly. There's also plenty of seating and space for hanging out on the side when not playing and some televisions with sports programming.

If interested in learning more about the place, here's the website: www.readytogolf.com

Hope you'll join us for our sixth ping pong event. Questions, comments, concerns or having trouble finding us? You can message Andy Milone on Meetup, or call/text him at 201-234-9609.

If interested, check out one of our many other events. We do bowling, volleyball, tennis, soccer, hiking, martial arts, billiards, dancing and bar crawls: [www.meetup.com/north-jersey-bowling-soccer-volleyball](https://www.meetup.com/north-jersey-bowling-soccer-volleyball)

title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**

title: Meeting at the Verona inn!
description:
Board Game Night At Verona Inn
We will be doing our first monthly meeting starting on **February 25th at the Verona Inn!** We will be meeting up to organize games starting at 7:30, with food and drinks available courtesy of our host! You can play any game provided by hosts or bring your own! If you do not have a friend group to play games, hosts will organize you into pods with other people who need players. There are **no dues**. Future meetings will be held on the **last Wednesday of each month.**

More information and ground rules:

* **The doors open at 6:30 but games do not start until 7:30.** I *highly recommend* coming in during this period to eat your food and drink ahead of time!
* **Please return the graciousness provided by our hosts and order at least one item! All venue specific rules apply to our club.** Future meetings depend on treating our hosts with respect.
* **All games must be returned to their owners when they announce that they are leaving.** If you are in a game in progress when the meeting ends but it is not borrowed you may continue playing!
* **Please place food and drink on a separate table or surface from your games** to help avoid stains and other damage.
* **Please engage with others in good faith, sportsmanship, respect and common sense.** *ABSOLUTELY NO harassment, getting physical, hurtful insulting, and persecutory language will be tolerated.* Repeat violators of venue rules AND/OR this rule may be asked to leave the event and not return.
